subject: Integration & Observability: SDK/Auth/Routing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@fintechco.com>, Ruth Alvarez <ruth.alvarez@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Integration & Observability: SDK/Auth/Routing follow-up

Hi Sam & Ruth —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking through FintechCo's use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

What we heard (high level):
- Primary workloads: conversational assistant for customer support + semantic search over transaction docs (embedding index + reranker).
- Expected steady-state: ~50 req/s for chat flows, embedding ingestion: 2000 docs/day, peak chat spikes to ~120 req/s.
- Latency sensitivity: support flows target p95 < 250ms for token generation.

Action items / asks from FintechCo:
1) Architecture diagram of how you're routing user traffic to the assistant and any proxy layers (can you attach?).
2) SDK language preferences and runtime constraints (Node/Go/Java).
3) Auth approach: API keys, short-lived tokens, or mutual TLS? Any KMS/HSM requirements?
4) Observability needs: you mentioned wanting trace-level linkage between user request and generated tokens — can you confirm the correlation id you use?

What we'll provide next:
- SDK quickstart tailored for Node.js + server-side Node agent with example headers for trace propagation and latency breakdown.
- Recommended embedding model & reranker based on your throughput profile.
- Sandbox instance with a sample dashboard showing per-route latency breakdown and token cost.

Proposed timeline:
- You send architecture diagram + preferred SDK (by EOD Friday)
- We provision sandbox + share dashboard access (within 48 hours after diagram)
- Follow-up technical call to walk SDK quickstart and auth flows (pick a time next week)

Attachments: please attach the architecture diagram if available.

Thanks — happy to loop in Dev to discuss dedicated capacity recommendations if your peak spike tolerance needs guaranteed throughput.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ruth Alvarez <ruth.alvarez@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration & Observability: SDK/Auth/Routing follow-up

Thanks Marissa — great summary. Attaching a current architecture diagram (fintechco-arch-diagram.pdf). A few clarifications from our side: 

- Primary runtime: Node.js (server-side microservice). Client-side web app calls our proxy which enriches user context then calls the assistant.
- Auth: we prefer short-lived API keys minted from our KMS, rotating every 12 hours. We can also support signed JWTs if needed. No mTLS for this phase.
- Routing: prefer low-latency path for chat (latency SLO higher priority than unit cost). Embeddings ingestion can be batched off-hours.
- Embeddings/reranker: yes — we'll do embeddings for search and a lightweight reranker to boost relevancy. Can you recommend which embedding model and a reranker setup for ~200ms additional processing?

Also: can you share any standard field names you expect in logs for correlating requests (trace id header name)? That will help our observability team wire up logs.

Thanks —
Sam Lee
Senior PM, Search & Assist
Sam.Lee@fintechco.com

(attachment: fintechco-arch-diagram.pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration & Observability: SDK/Auth/Routing follow-up

Great, thanks for the diagram and the details — really helpful. Quick answers and a few concrete pointers below.

SDK / Auth
- We have first-class SDKs for Node.js and Go. For Node.js we'll send a quickstart with server-side examples that use short-lived API keys.
- Example auth flow: mint short-lived key client side against your auth service -> attach x-redwood-api-key header on server calls.

Observability headers (recommended)
- Trace correlation header: X-Redwood-Trace-Id (we'll honor your correlation id if you send X-Fintechco-Correlation-Id; we include both in logs).
- Latency breakdown header (returned): X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown — a compact CSV of latency buckets: total, queuing, kernel, io, kv-cache-hit. Example: total=130ms;queue=10ms;kernel=80ms;io=30ms;kv_cache_hit=true
- Request id header (response): X-Redwood-Request-Id — include in logs for quick lookup in dashboard.

Structured output & tool calling
- If you'll be invoking external tools or actions, we support structured tool calling with explicit JSON schema in the response. We'll provide example JSON schema and safe execution pattern in the SDK quickstart.

Embeddings & Reranker
- Recommendation based on scale: redwood-embed-3-small for embeddings (good throughput/quality for your doc sizes) and redwood-rerank-1 for light reranking.
- For your throughput: batched ingestion (100-500 docs/batch) during off-peak will keep costs low; consider incremental updates for changed docs only.

Next deliverables (today):
- Attaching Node.js SDK quickstart + example pipeline (redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf).
- I'll provision a sandbox workspace and add Sam & Ruth with read-only dashboard access (sandbox invite in a separate file).
- Propose a technical sync Tue 2026-03-10 10:00 PT — is that OK?

Sample Node.js header snippet (server):
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'x-redwood-api-key': process.env.REDWOOD_KEY,
    'X-Redwood-Trace-Id': req.headers['x-fintechco-correlation-id'] || generateId(),
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-chat-3', prompt: userPrompt })
});

I'll loop Dev on capacity/throughput planning.

—
Marissa
(attachment: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf)

Hi Sam — looping in on recommended infra:

- Given the 120 req/s peak, if you need strict p95 latency SLAs we recommend Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) to avoid noisy-neighbor effects.
- For embeddings ingestion I recommend a small batching service (we can share our reference pipeline) and a warm KV-cache tier for hot documents to reduce kernel time.
- I'll prep an estimate for committed throughput vs burst capacity and send by EOD Monday.

If you'd like to start on Hosted Sandbox first, we can do that immediately and then evaluate Dedicated once you have traffic patterns.

Thanks,
Dev
Infra & Performance | Redwood Inference
